mappings.note: Where the birds fly (the boundless sky) -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-118: stated.

What the poet means by the three absences -- greed, sin, care: keyed as freedom from any avarice or worldly anxiety, a reading past the words. Rejected LO-121, used for the bare 'what do they lack' item.
Purport of the line about not wanting to seize the world's wealth -- his claim about contentment. Rejected LO-124: a whole line's argument.
Where all the birds live together (the forest). Rejected LO-118: stated.
What the extract calls the birds' home (the sky). Rejected LO-118, kept for the item asking what that implies.
Where the birds sleep at night (in the trees). Rejected LO-118: stated.
Which birds live in the forest -- the extract's list. Rejected LO-124: names collected, not glossed.
How the birds live together -- with affection, as the extract has it. Rejected LO-118: stated.
Through whom the poet gives his message (the chidiya) -- recognising her as his vehicle. Rejected LO-121: the poem does not say she is his device.
Where the chidiya sits -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-115: a fact, not a rendering.
What she tells in her speech, keyed simply as 'some message'. Rejected LO-118, kept for the items that read what the message is.
The lesson's name and the poet's -- bibliographic placement. Rejected LO-121: not inside the verse.

Which question the POET puts to us -- do you know what message she gives? The item turns on the question the text asks in order to make the reader think, which is what this outcome covers. Rejected LO-118: the question, not the answer he implies.
Where the chidiya is seated in this extract. Rejected LO-115: a fact.
The likely sense of 'sandesh' in this poem's context -- a precept of love and goodwill. The item asks what one word carries here. Rejected LO-118: lexical before it is conceptual.
Who inspires one to be free and selfless (the chidiya) -- the agent, located. Rejected LO-118: attribution.

Where and when the song is heard AND how the SCENE feels -- the second half asks the learner to render the atmosphere in their own words, which is what this outcome covers. Rejected LO-121, which fits only the locating half.

What the poet expects of man through that line -- keyed as wanting him curious about nature's subtle signs, i.e. to question in order to understand better. Rejected LO-118: the expectation is about enquiry itself.

Which birds this extract names. Rejected LO-124: the names are collected, not glossed. NOTE: the key gives kauaa, hans, tota, which are the plain-Hindi equivalents of the poem's kaak, hans and shuk rather than its own words.
What the birds' living 'hilmil' SHOWS -- unity and harmony, an inference. Rejected LO-121, used for the bare 'how do they live' item.
Which trait 'jahaan chaahte, jaate hain' signals (freedom) -- read off the line. Rejected LO-121: the trait is inferred.
How the different birds behave to one another -- living and eating together, stated in the extract. Rejected LO-118, kept for the item asking what that shows.
The sense of 'the sky is their home' AND how it shapes their life -- the poet's claim about boundlessness. Rejected LO-121, used for the bare 'where is their home' item.
Which feeling the poet asks man to give up, keyed as enmity and rancour -- glossing 'droh'. Rejected LO-116: the item asks the word's sense, not the learner's view on social division.
What the chidiya comes to tell on the peepal branch -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-118, kept for items that read the message out.
What her sitting, startling us and flying off SHOWS -- keyed as her fleeting presence, an inference. Rejected LO-121: the actions are stated, the reading is not.

What 'droh-bhaavna against humanity' means and why he urges giving it up -- his reasoning that it opposes love and unity. Rejected LO-116: the key stays at enmity and inhumanity in general and does not put caste, religion or gender to the learner.
With what purpose she seems to come and sing -- the poet's design, inferred. Rejected LO-121: no line states a purpose.
In whose minds greed, sin and care are absent (the birds') -- located in the extract. Rejected LO-118: attribution.
Which trait the line about not seizing the world's wealth shows -- contentment and selflessness, inferred. Rejected LO-121, used where the line is only located.
How the birds feed themselves (by their own labour) -- stated in the extract. Rejected LO-118: no inference.

Which three negative feelings the birds are free of, and what man can learn -- the second half is the poet's lesson. Rejected LO-121 because of that. NOTE: the key names lobh, moh and eershya, whereas the poem's three are lobh, paap and parvaah, which two other items in this chapter key correctly -- so this key is wrong.
The purport of the 'chaah nahin' line and how it expresses the birds' philosophy of life -- the poet's claim about taking only what is needed. Rejected LO-124: more than a gloss is asked.
